tool.name: TransVar
tool.description: annotates genomic, cDNA and protein variants
tool.command:
## The generated config holds the reference and the database paths, so the ## command line only has to name which of them to switch on. TRANSVAR_CFG also ## keeps TransVar away from the config inside its installed Python package. export TRANSVAR_CFG='$transvar_cfg' && ## TransVar resolves a database it cannot open relative to this directory, and ## crashes in posixpath.join when the variable is unset. export TRANSVAR_DOWNLOAD_DIR='$annotations.fields.path' &&
transvar $annotation.mode --refversion '$annotations.fields.refversion' #for $source in str($sources).split(',') --$source #end for #if str($annotation.input_type.query_source) == 'text' -i '$annotation.input_type.query' #elif str($annotation.input_type.query_source) == 'file' -l '$annotation.input_type.query_file' #else --vcf '$annotation.input_type.query_vcf' #end if $adv.transcript_selection $adv.strictversion $adv.gseq $adv.aa3 $adv.oneline --seqmax $adv.seqmax --prombeg $adv.prombeg --promend $adv.promend #if str($annotation.input_type.query_source) == 'vcf' > '$output_vcf' #else > '$output' #end if

param.name: mode
param.label: Annotation mode
param.help: Which level the variants you want to annotate are expressed on.

param.name: query_source
param.label: Variants to annotate
param.option: Read a list of variants from a dataset
Read variants from a VCF dataset

param.name: query_vcf
param.label: VCF dataset
param.help: The annotation is appended as extra columns to each record.

param.name: annotations
param.label: Transcript annotation database
param.help: Downloaded with the TransVar data manager.

validator.message: No TransVar annotation database is available. Ask your Galaxy administrator to run the TransVar data manager.

param.name: sources
param.label: Transcript annotation sources
param.help: TransVar reports one line per matching transcript, so selecting several sources annotates the same variant against each of them.

validator.message: The selected database contains no annotation sources.

param.name: reference
param.label: Reference genome
param.help: TransVar reads the reference sequence to resolve codons and to check reference alleles. Pick the assembly the annotation database above was built for; a mismatched genome yields wrong consequences or no output at all.

validator.message: No reference genome is available. Ask your Galaxy administrator to install the assembly the annotation database was built for.

param.name: transcript_selection
param.label: Transcripts to consider
param.option: Protein-coding transcript with the longest CDS only

param.label: Require matching transcript version
param.help: Only match a queried transcript accession if its version number is identical.

param.label: Append VCF-style coordinates
param.help: Adds CHROM, POS, REF and ALT columns to the output.

param.label: Use three letter amino acid codes
One line per query
param.help: Collapse the hits of all matching transcripts into a single line.

param.label: Maximum reported sequence length
param.help: Longer reference or alternative sequences are abbreviated. Use -1 to report them in full.

param.label: Promoter start
param.help: Bases upstream of the transcription start site that still count as promoter.

param.label: Promoter end
param.help: Bases downstream of the transcription start site that still count as promoter.

tool.help:
**What it does**
TransVar_ is a multiway annotator for precision medicine. It translates a variant between the genomic, cDNA and protein levels and reports, for every matching transcript, the affected region and the functional consequence.
Pick the level your variants are written on:
* **Protein level (panno)**, e.g. ``PIK3CA:p.E545K`` * **cDNA level (canno)**, e.g. ``PIK3CA:c.1633G>A`` * **Genomic level (ganno)**, e.g. ``chr3:g.178936091G>A``
Variants can be typed one at a time into the form, read line by line from a dataset, or, in genomic mode, taken from a VCF dataset. VCF input produces VCF output with the annotation appended as extra columns; every other input produces a tabular dataset.
-----
**Transcript annotation databases**
The transcript sets are not bundled with TransVar. A Galaxy administrator downloads them once with the **TransVar annotations** data manager, which stores them in a Galaxy managed data directory. This tool then reads them from there, rather than from the installed Python package.
Selecting more than one source annotates each variant against each of them; the ``source`` field of the ``info`` column says which transcript set a line came from.
-----
**Reference genome**
TransVar reads the reference sequence to resolve codons and to verify reference alleles, so a reference genome is always required. It must be the assembly the annotation database was built for, otherwise the reported consequences are wrong. Without a matching reference TransVar reports no annotation at all.
The genome is taken from the assemblies your administrator has installed, rather than from a dataset in your history. TransVar's transcript databases are published only for a few assemblies (hg19, hg38 and mm10), and the same administrator who runs the data manager to install them also installs the matching genome, so pairing the two from the same curated lists avoids silently annotating against the wrong assembly.
-----
**Output**
One line per query and matching transcript, with the input, the transcript and gene, the coordinates on all three levels, the affected region, and an ``info`` field holding the consequence (``CSQN``), the reference codon, candidate alternative codons and the annotation source.
.. _TransVar: https://bioinformatics.mdanderson.org/public-software/transvar/
